headline: High-risk default write-capable RAG agent can cascade errors and leak sensitive data when paired with OpenBB's MCP-connected finance workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes files/APIs, while production-agentic-rag-course runs a LangGraph subagent with file and API surfaces. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge is not explicitly documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than proven. If B ingests A's outputs as trusted text, prompt injection is plausible.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through a shared MCP server or copied outputs
IF B treats A-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the agents
Wrap A outputs in a strict schema before B reads them
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Review B prompts for instruction-following over file content
requires-engineering: isolate the agents in separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches financial, licensed, and public data and can use MCP; B reads and writes files and handles configuration secrets. No shared workspace is documented, but if they share a local environment or copied artifacts, sensitive finance or secret material can flow from A into B's outputs or logs. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local workspace or copied files
IF B logs or summarizes inputs containing financial data or secrets
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate directories
Remove secrets from any shared artifacts before handoff
Turn off verbose logging for B
Audit B outputs for accidental secret echoing
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write plus shell/subprocess execution, while A can use MCP and multiple instances. Even though A cannot write files itself, the pair can still contend over shared mutable resources if A's MCP-connected workflows and B's local development environment touch the same paths. Because shared locking is not stated, uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or project directory
IF A's MCP-connected workflow and B's shell commands mutate overlapping files
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared config files
Use file locks for any shared artifacts
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's agentic RAG workflow can consume upstream outputs, and A is a financial-modeling agent whose outputs may be treated as authoritative facts. If B uses A's results without verification, errors can cascade into downstream content or actions. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A's outputs as source material for generated answers
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require citation checks before B reuses A outputs
Add a validation step for numeric finance claims
Mark A outputs as untrusted input in B prompts
Sample-check a few downstream responses for drift
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware routing

E_compliance.rationale: A handles financial and licensed data, while B handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment with Docker/Airflow credentials. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so this is not high; however, differing retention and secret-handling practices can still create compliance gaps if the same data class is shared.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is copied into B's local development environment
IF either agent retains logs or artifacts longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's dev environment
Rotate any exposed secrets immediately
Set short log retention on both agents
Document which data classes each agent may process
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
